title: Golf Elbow Rehab Program
tagline: 4-Week Plan to Reduce Pain and Restore Strength

callouts: Targets the inside of the elbow (Medial Epicondylitis)

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.notes:
CALM PAIN. START HEALING.
- Reduce irritation
- Begin tendon remodeling
- Restore function
WEEK 1 FOCUS:
- Eccentric lengthening of the wrist extensors
- Reduce inflammation
- Maintain mobility
- Begin building tendon tolerance
ADDITIONAL TIPS FOR WEEK 1:
- Use a light weight (1-2 lbs).
- Do exercises 2-3× per day.
- Ice 15-20 minutes after any activity.
- Use heat 2-6 hours in the evening.
- Stay consistent every day.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Heavy lifting or gripping
- Repetitive wrist flexion or twisting (e.g., heavy golf, wrenching)
- Pain-provoking activities — modify as needed
weeks.editorNotes: Labels removed from notes: "Week banner:" (around the banner slogan) and "Banner icons:" (before the icon list).

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extensions
exercises.whenToUse: Targets the wrist extensors to rehab the tendon.
focus: Palm down (knuckles up)
Keep your forearm supported on a table or your thigh
Move slowly — 3-4 seconds on the way down
Full range of motion (let the weight pull your wrist down as far as comfortable)
Use 1-2 lb weight (start light)
steps: Start at the top. Use a light weight (1-2 lbs). Help up with your other hand if needed.
Slowly lower down with the affected arm (eccentric) over 3-4 seconds.
Go through full range of motion. Then use your other hand to help lift back up and repeat.

exercises.name: Ice After Activity
howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes
After exercises, sports (golf), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.notes:
INCREASE LOAD. DEEPEN THE STRETCH.
- Build tendon tolerance
- Improve strength and control
- Reduce pain and prevent recurrence
WEEK 2 FOCUS:
- Continue eccentric lengthening of the wrist extensors
- Increase repetitions and/or resistance
- Add a wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom of each rep
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 2 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Increase to 3-4 lbs (if Week 1 was 1-2 lbs).
- Increase to 2-3 sets of 15 reps.
- Always include the wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom.
- Ice immediately after activity.
- Use heat in the evening for 2-6 hours.
- Stay consistent daily.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Heavy lifting or gripping
- Repetitive wrist flexion or twisting
- Pain-provoking activities
- Golf with poor technique or excessive volume

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extensions + Flexion Squeeze
exercises.whenToUse: Lengthens and strengthens the wrist extensors while improving flexibility.
focus: Full range of motion
Lower slowly (3-4 seconds)
Add a gentle wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom
Keep your forearm supported
Use a weight that is challenging but allows good form
No pain during or after (except mild discomfort)

other.Load: Use 3-4 lb weight (or increase from Week 1)

steps: Start at the top. Hold a moderate weight (3-4 lbs). Palm down. Support your forearm on your thigh or a table.
Slowly lower down (eccentric) over 3-4 seconds to full wrist flexion.
At the bottom, perform a gentle wrist flexion squeeze for 1-2 seconds to further stretch the wrist extensors.

exercises.name: Ice After Activity
howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes.
After exercise, sports (golf), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.notes:
ADD STRENGTH. CONTROL BOTH DIRECTIONS.
- Build strength and tendon capacity
- Add light concentric work
- Improve endurance and function
WEEK 3 FOCUS:
- Continue eccentric lengthening of the wrist extensors
- Add a light concentric (lifting) phase
- Maintain the wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom of each rep
- Increase resistance (typically 3-4 lbs) and/or repetitions
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 3 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Increase to 3-4 lbs (if Week 2 was 1-2 lbs).
- Add the concentric (lifting) phase with a light weight (1-2 lbs).
- Maintain the wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom.
- Ice after activity (15-20 minutes).
- Heat in the evening (2-6 hours).
- Stay consistent 2-3× per day.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Heavy lifting or gripping
- Repetitive wrist flexion or twisting
- Pain-provoking activities
- Golf with poor technique or excessive volume

exercises.name: Wrist Extensions with Concentric + Eccentric
exercises.whenToUse: Strengthens the wrist extensors and builds tendon tolerance.
focus: Full range of motion
Lift up (concentric) with light weight and good control (1-2 seconds)
Lower down (eccentric) slowly over 3-4 seconds
Perform a gentle wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom
Focus on controlled movement — no swinging
Use a weight that is challenging but allows good form

other.Load: Use 3-4 lb weight (or increase from Week 2)

steps: Start at the bottom. Wrist relaxed and slightly flexed (stretch position). Squeeze gently.
Concentric (up): Slowly lift the weight up through full range of motion (1-2 seconds). Use a light weight (1-2 lbs).
Pause at the top. Squeeze for 1 second.
Eccentric (down): Slowly lower over 3-4 seconds. At the bottom, perform a gentle wrist flexion squeeze for 1-2 seconds.

exercises.name: Ice After Activity
howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes.
After exercise, sports (golf), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

weeks.label: Week 4
weeks.notes:
BUILD STRENGTH. RETURN TO ACTIVITY.
- Restore strength and endurance
- Improve control and function
- Prepare for return to golf and daily use
WEEK 4 FOCUS:
- Continue eccentric and concentric wrist extensions
- Increase resistance (5-6 lbs for eccentric, 1-2 lbs for concentric)
- Maintain wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom of each rep
- Build strength and endurance
- Continue ice after activity and heat in the evening
WEEK 4 TIPS FOR SUCCESS:
- Use 5-6 lb for eccentric (down) reps.
- Use 1-2 lb for concentric (up) reps.
- Work up to 15-20 reps per set.
- Keep the wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom.
- Ice after activity (15-20 minutes).
- Heat in the evening (2-6 hours).
- Begin return to golf and normal activity as pain allows.
AVOID FOR NOW:
- Heavy lifting or gripping
- Repetitive wrist flexion or twisting
- Pain-provoking activities
- Golf with poor technique or excessive volume

exercises.name: Wrist Extensions (Full Program)
exercises.whenToUse: Perform both concentric (up) and eccentric (down) with a wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom.
focus: Full range of motion
Use a heavier weight for the eccentric (down) and a lighter weight for the concentric (up)
Wrist flexion squeeze at the bottom of each rep
Controlled movement (neither fast nor jerky)
Increase reps toward 20 if comfortable
Stop if sharp pain (mild discomfort is okay)
steps: Start at the bottom. Wrist relaxed and slightly flexed (stretch position). Squeeze gently.
Concentric (up): Use a light weight (1-2 lbs). Lift through full range of motion in 1-2 seconds.
Pause at the top. Squeeze for 1 second. Keep control.
Eccentric (down): Use a heavier weight (5-6 lbs). Lower slowly over 3-4 seconds. At the bottom, perform a gentle wrist flexion squeeze for 1-2 seconds.

howTo: Use an ice pack or ice massage.
15-20 minutes.
After exercise, sports (golf), typing, phone use, or any prolonged forearm activity.
You can repeat multiple times throughout the day.

exercises.name: Heat in the Evening
exercises.whenToUse: Increases blood flow and promotes healing.
howTo: Use a heating pad or warm compress.
2-6 hours at the end of the day (after all activity).
Keep it comfortable (warm, not hot).

Clinical content check for Dr. Caban: golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis) normally involves the wrist FLEXORS, but every golf-elbow sheet targets the wrist EXTENSORS (palm down), while the tennis-elbow sheets target the flexors. Transcribed verbatim; the two programs may be swapped on the source sheets.
sourceNotes: Read golfers-elbow-4 Week 1-4 sheets (Drive ids as listed per week). All four sheets present, no duplicates. Each sheet: header (MD FIT logo, condition title, 4-week tagline, target callout), week banner with headline + 3 icon goals, WEEK N FOCUS box with anatomy illustration, card 1 = the strengthening exercise (picture captions + SETS & REPS / SETS, REPS & LOAD box + KEY POINTS), card 2 = Ice After Activity, card 3 = Heat in the Evening (both with HOW TO DO IT bullets), bottom row = tips strip + AVOID FOR NOW. Field mapping: each card's one-line subtitle (purpose line under the title) is stored in whenToUse; KEY POINTS -> focus; picture captions -> steps; HOW TO DO IT bullets -> howTo; week banner headline -> week focus; banner icons, WEEK N FOCUS bullets, tips strip and AVOID FOR NOW list -> week notes (they differ week to week). Header text is printed in ALL CAPS; titles/names converted to title case. En dashes in ranges converted to ASCII hyphens; em dashes kept. No GOAL box, key principles, daily basics or progression overview exist on these sheets, so those fields are empty.
